The court will most likely require a greater foundation (answer B). Computer business records qualify under the business-records exception only if a custodian or other qualified witness establishes how they are made and kept and that the computer process is reliable, and the defendant's bare statement that he kept them regularly doesn't do that. The team note is wrong as a general rule: a declarant's availability doesn't remove hearsay status, since Rule 801(d)(1) covers only certain prior statements of a testifying witness, and Rule 803 applies regardless of availability, so option C fails.

CONFIDENCE: 82
